title: $4000 Bike Build Challenge! Kung Vs VFV

takeaways.text: The size M Mach build with electronic shifting, tubeless tires, an 800 g crank and pedals weighed 7.93 kg.
The retailer put the Mach frameset at about US$1,399 in July 2026.

After about four months and 1,000 km: very stiff under power and planted in hard cornering, best on flat and rolling routes rather than long climbs; it felt harsh on tubes until he switched to tubeless.

The size M seat angle is 73.5°, about 0.5° slacker than the Tarmac and Quick Pro ER:ONE they compared; the aero seatpost has only a 10 mm offset and KUNG had no zero-offset post yet, so he moved to a long-nose saddle.
The rider ranks its ride quality around a Winspace T1500 and below the more refined, pricier Quick Pro ER:ONE.

disclosure: China Cycling sells both frames compared in the video and says so; the Kung Mach build is a staff member's own bike.
summary: Retailer's US$4,000 aero-build challenge: a size M KUNG Mach with electronic shifting ridden for four months and about 1,000 km, compared with a VFV Echo.
